[Chorus: female gospel-soul voice, choir answering]
We save you a plate (every Sunday)
Your chair's still yours (at the head)
We say your grace the way you said it
We pass your cornbread
Till I see you again, till I pull up to that gate
Mama, we save you a plate

[Verse 1: male rap, gentle, direct address]
Four o'clock. I got the big pot out, the dented one
Your recipe's a napkin and it's faded in the sun
I called your sister twice to ask how much is "some"
She laughed and cried and said, "Baby, till it's done"
Kids set the table, put a fork down at your spot
Nobody told them to. They just know what's what.
I tried to say the blessing and my voice went thin
Your grandson finished it. He sounds like you. He grinned.

[Chorus: female gospel-soul voice, choir answering]
We save you a plate (every Sunday)
Your chair's still yours (at the head)
We say your grace the way you said it
We pass your cornbread
Till I see you again, till I pull up to that gate
Mama, we save you a plate

[Verse 2: rap, steadier, strings in]
You raised four of us on one check and a prayer
Worked the early shift and still did all our hair
I never saw you sit until the last of us was fed
Then you'd eat standing at the counter. That's what you did.
I'm fifty and I only now can see the cost
I'd give a year to tell you nothing that you gave was lost
The house is loud. The baby's got your laugh.
We're alright, Mama. You did that. Do the math.

[Bridge: quartet in harmony, organ rising]
There's a table where you are
Longer than this one, set with stars
Save me a seat like I save yours

[Final Chorus: full choir, voice soaring]

Your chair's still yours (at the head)
We say your grace the way you said it
We pass your cornbread
Till I see you again, till I pull up to that gate
Mama, we save you a plate
